clue.text: His bolt " fell upon a little western flower " said Oberon

definitions.text: His bolt " fell upon a little western flower " said Oberon

parts.words: His bolt " fell upon a little western flower " said Oberon
parts.note: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Oberon tells Puck where the love god's arrow landed, turning a pansy into a love potion; the bolt is the archer's arrow

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's fairy king about where an arrow came down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love shoots arrows that make people fall in love; Oberon describes one of his darts striking a flower.

clue.text: 22 dn material for Kings, Queens and others

definitions.text: 22 dn material for Kings, Queens and others

parts.words: 22 dn material for Kings, Queens and others
parts.note: kings and queens here are playing cards, and 22 down gives BASIC: the plain stiff stuff such cards are printed on

explanation.surface: A question about what royalty is made of at bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing cards such as kings and queens are printed on stiff pasteboard, the basic material of a pack.

clue.text: Alias Simon. Simple!

definitions.meaning: the apostle Simon was renamed by Jesus, so his other name is the rock-name
... Simple is the title of a novel by Captain Marryat, so the name completes 'Simple'

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a false name is easily explained.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle known as Simon took the name meaning rock, and Marryat's naive naval hero is called by it too.

clue.text: Power house

definitions.meaning: a ruling family holds power over a country
a royal house is a line of rulers, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Two words that look like an electricity station.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of rulers from one family, such as the Ming or Tudors, is both a power and a royal house.

clue.text: Philatelist, for instance, instructing Olympic athlete ?

annotationWithheld.why: Philatelist, for instance, instructing Olympic athlete ? (9): 'Philatelist, for instance' defines COLLECTOR, but no parse of 'instructing Olympic athlete' giving the letters or a second sense could be found

clue.text: Head cook's taking in one of the head -men

indicators.note: taking in means the cook's word swallows the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a chef is the head cook in a kitchen; the possessive gives the S
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The kitchen boss enlists one of the senior staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders or headmen of a tribe or group are its chiefs.

clue.text: Subsidence announced from the crow's-nest?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the ground sinking is a ...
the lookout at the masthead calls out when the coast is first sighted from sea

explanation.surface: A sailor on watch reports the ground giving way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighting or reaching shore after a voyage is making landfall, and land falling is subsidence.

clue.text: He can make trouble at home. So restrain him ?

indicators.note: to make trouble is to stir things up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A troublemaker in the household should be tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'So restrain him?' as advice about a troublemaker; only 'restrain' defines, and 'make trouble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in chains is to restrain or fetter them.

clue.text: Tangent makes a sporting boundary

definitions.meaning: in geometry a tangent is a straight stroke that grazes a curve at one point
the side boundary of a football or rugby pitch

explanation.surface: A geometry term doubling as the edge of a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent just touches a curve, and the side boundary of a football or rugby pitch has the same name.

clue.text: Straight man in 3 dn ?

definitions.meaning: 3 down is DYNASTY, and the person at the head of a dynasty reigns over it

explanation.surface: A comedian's stooge belongs to a ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring straight-edge and a monarch of a dynasty share the name.

clue.text: Holding one or two nets perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given may be arranged some other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: two asks for the word for a net to be written twice

parts.note: nets gives a single net, used twice

explanation.surface: A fisherman holding one or two nets.
explanation.walkthrough: I, OR and NET twice (from 'two nets') make IORNETNET, which 'perhaps' shuffles into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the keeping or holding of something.

clue.text: Rustic as leader of Caledonian fling

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Caledonian is used

parts.note: to fling is to hurl

explanation.surface: A country fellow leads a Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A Highland fling is a Scottish dance, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a peasant or boorish rustic.

clue.text: Congregation proverbially assembled

parts.note: the proverb says that those alike flock together, so the gathering is of like-minded folk

explanation.surface: A church gathering described with a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about creatures of one plumage flocking together describes like-minded people who congregate.

clue.text: Invariably people say every avenue "

indicators.note: what people say is a spoken version, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: every avenue or route is all ways

explanation.surface: People claim the same thing down every road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens invariably happens at all times, without exception.

clue.text: Want a keep rebuilt in part of old Yorkshire

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A castle tower needs reconstructing somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: A wapentake was an old administrative division of Yorkshire and other northern counties, like a hundred elsewhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Danelaw counties, including Yorkshire, a wapentake was a historic subdivision of a shire.

clue.text: Conflict about pub turn that's exclusively Scottish?

indicators.note: about means the conflict word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a conflict is a clash

indicators.note: turn means the pub word is read backwards

parts.note: a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in a bar over something purely Scottish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the pub word and 'about' wraps the conflict around it; the question mark admits clans are a Scottish example of exclusiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish clans are close-knit groups, and being exclusive in that way is to be cliquish.

clue.text: He will point to the club menace as a stinker sometimes

parts.note: he will contracts to he'll
E, east, is a point of the compass
the club bore is the tiresome member everyone avoids

explanation.surface: A man promises to identify the nuisance at his club.
explanation.walkthrough: One species is called the stinking hellebore, hence 'a stinker sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant has one species named for its foul smell, so it is sometimes a stinker.

clue.text: Lacking which Daisy's marriage lacks 27

parts.note: the music-hall song Daisy Bell says the wedding won't be stylish because the singer can't afford a horse-drawn vehicle; 27 across is STYLE

explanation.surface: A riddle about why someone's wedding will be a plain affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell ('Daisy, Daisy') is a Victorian song: 'It won't be a stylish marriage, I can't afford a ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, the couple can't afford a horse-drawn coach, so the wedding has no style.

clue.text: Degree paper, first of ten for an ambassador

parts.note: the certificate recording a degree is a diploma

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of ten is taken

explanation.surface: A graduate with a top certificate is fit to be an envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior envoy in a country's foreign service.

clue.text: Moor's pre-Christian greeting

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, covers the period before Christ
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A North African's salutation from before Christ's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Othello is subtitled the Moor of Venice; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tragic hero of Shakespeare's play is a Moorish general.

clue.text: One not entirely satisfied with patriotism

definitions.text: One not entirely satisfied with patriotism

parts.words: One not entirely satisfied with patriotism
parts.note: the British nurse executed in 1915 said before her death that patriotism is not enough

explanation.surface: Someone finds love of country falls short.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War nurse Edith said on the eve of execution that patriotism was not enough.

clue.text: Abused a maker of early music pieces

indicators.note: the clue's letters are the raw stuff from which the answer is made, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mistreated a composer of early music.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or tune for the dawn, so these are early-morning music pieces.

clue.text: God! The lady's embracing me!

indicators.note: embracing means the lady's word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: the lady's is hers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man exclaims as a woman hugs him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek messenger of the gods is a deity of Olympus.

clue.text: Patience. But the post was never filled

definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience has an alternative title naming the poet's intended

definitions.text: But the post was never filled
definitions.meaning: the poet Bunthorne ends the opera alone, so no woman ever took the role of his wife

explanation.surface: Someone counsels patience about a job that stayed vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta has the subtitle naming the poet's wife-to-be, who never materialised.

clue.text: Sort of English when over one hundred degrees

indicators.note: in a down answer, the degrees come over, that is above, the rest

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A kind of English spoken when it is extremely hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Basic English is a simplified 850-word form of English devised by C. K. Ogden.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden's simplified version of the language, with a small core vocabulary, is called Basic English.

clue.text: One's Song of the Island

parts.note: one is I, and the possessive gives S
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A ballad about an island, sung by oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the Hebridean islands off western Scotland.

clue.text: Whiting's slow-moving companion

parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the whiting urges a sluggish creature to walk a little faster

explanation.surface: A fish has a dawdling friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's Lobster Quadrille, the whiting tells a slow shelled creature to walk a little faster.

clue.text: Member has trouble 'taking in sick animal

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: taking in means the trouble word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A club member has bother looking after an ailing pet.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas is an animal.

clue.text: Indians, dear to Frenchmen, look for nothing in return

parts.note: cher is French for dear

indicators.note: in return means the words for look for and nothing are read backwards together

parts.note: to look for is to seek
O is the zero-shaped letter for nothing

explanation.surface: Native Americans that Frenchmen love expect nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns the look-for word and the nothing letter together, as one run backwards, giving OKEES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Native American people, once called Indians, originally of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Fashion unpopular with lame dogs, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that what counts is how the word sounds, not its spelling

parts.note: the saying is to help a lame dog over a stile, a step in a fence a hurt dog cannot climb

explanation.surface: A trend that limping dogs dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is fashion, a current mode of dress or design.
